thread:
alex: heads-up — noticed a p95 decode latency regression after yesterday's runtime merge (commit 3b7f2c9). p50 mostly stable, but p95 jumped ~35% on shortseq workload :grimacing:

sam: which shortseq profile? internal/shortseq-1k or prod traffic? :eyes:

alex: prod shortseq (avg tokens ~12). observed on dedicated infra in canary region. baseline before merge p95 ~42ms, after merge ~57ms. tail spike around token 3-6 of decode.

maria: interesting — token-3..6 suggests kernel selection change at early decode. did the merge touch kernel heuristics or warmup affinity?

alex: merge was the fused-attn scheduling rewrite (PR #5123). main change: more aggressive prefetch for batched matmuls + a small tweak to kernel selector weight for small seqs.

jen: ci-bot reports perf regression on e2e-decode-shortseq in CI too, run 2027-03-15_03:12. CI change says +28% p95 on model-rhino-7b quant.

ci-bot: perf-ci: job e2e-decode-shortseq failed threshold. p95 increased from 45ms -> 58ms. Trace available: https://ci.internal/perf/1719012345

sam: can you share a sampled trace or perf profile? flamegraphs would help to see where time moved.

alex: attaching quick perf snippet from perf-tool (reduced):

```
# top framediff (after - before)
decode_step  +32%  (kernels: attention_fused_dispatch)
attention_kernel_select +18% (selector: chose attn_transpose_opt on shortseq)
matmul_prefetch +40%
kv_cache_read +3%
```

alex: also saw increased device memcpy stalls around warmup windows. nvprof shows additional memcpy calls right before decode loop.

maria: that sounds like the prefetch scheduling is over-eager for small batches and triggers an extra memcopy path. maybe prefetch logic doesn't check small-seq fast path.

liam: I can reproduce locally on a dev box. Running shortseq benchmark with --seq=12 replicates p95 bump. Bisecting quickly to narrow commits.

liam: quick bisect update — revert candidate range narrowed to commits between 3b7f2c9..3b9d9e1 (the scheduling rewrite + selector tweak). Picking the selector tweak (3b9a3f2) as suspect.

sam: does the selector tweak flip on a weight threshold? If it biases attn_transpose_opt for seq<16, that would explain early-token path.

alex: yep it does. change introduced `if (seq_len < 16) score += 0.2` for attn_transpose_opt. The rationale was microbenchmarks for 8-12 seqs but maybe combined with prefetch change it's regressing.

jen: can we confirm whether attn_transpose_opt is slower in this config or if the overhead is from extra memcpy/prefetch interplay? We need a minimal repro: run with selector forced to previous kernel vs new kernel and compare.

liam: did that. forcing previous kernel (attn_fused_naive) drops p95 back to 44ms. forcing attn_transpose_opt yields 59ms. So transpose path slower in our full runtime context.

perf-bot: perf-check: attn_transpose_opt microbenchmarks standalone are 10% faster for seq<=12 on bench harness, but end-to-end with KV cache and prefetch it's 25% slower. Summary: kernel microbenchmarks don't cover memcopy/prefetch effects.

maria: aha — so the kernel choose plus prefetch scheduling interaction produces extra memcopies. The attn_transpose_opt probably expects prefetched contiguous blocks; the scheduling rewrite issues a redundant prefetch, leading to double-memcopy and stalls.

sam: plan: 1) revert the selector bias (3b9a3f2) as a minimal rollback, 2) add integration perf test covering prefetch+kernel combos, 3) instrument prefetch path to avoid duplicate memcopies when kernel will do its own copy. Anyone object?

jen: +1 to revert as an immediate mitigation. We should push a hotfix to canary and CI.

alex: I'll open the revert PR and attach the bisect notes. Also adding a short test harness patch to CI that forces prefetch path enabled + shortseq to prevent regressions.

liam: I'll prepare a small reproducer and a perf trace showing memcpy duplication (will paste under the issue).

maria: longer-term, we should update kernel selection scoring to be aware of prefetch semantics (a flag per kernel: expects_prefetch vs performs_internal_copy). That will avoid thrash.

sam: agreed. also add a perf-eval that runs fused-attn + prefetch in a single e2e test across sequence lengths [8,12,16,32].

ci-bot: deploy-canary job queued: revert PR #5178 (revert 3b9a3f2) will run canary in us-west-2.

alex: thanks. I'll monitor metrics and post updates here. If canary looks good after 30m we'll roll to prod.

jen: note for release notes: revert mention + follow-up to tune kernel scoring and prefetch idempotency.

perf-bot: follow-ups created: PERF-1243 (prefetch idempotency), PERF-1244 (selector scoring semantics), PERF-1245 (CI shortseq integration test).

alex: closing loop — initial canary shows p95 back to ~43ms at 30m. marking this thread resolved but will keep PERF tickets open. :thumbsup:
